Encrypted storage for users’ access and refresh tokens, read by the tool layer at call time so secrets never enter the prompt.
progressive disclosure
Loading only a short description up front and the full instructions or files when they are needed.
agent skill
A packaged folder of instructions, scripts and references that an agent loads when a task matches its description.

fcall.name: Process-Level Eval
fcall.note: Process evaluation scores tool calls after the fact; function calling is how each call is made and returned.

fcall.name: JSON Schema and Constrained Decoding
fcall.note: Strict tool use applies the same schema guarantee to tool arguments that structured outputs give to answers.

fcall.name: Code as Action (CodeAct)
fcall.note: Function calling sends one structured call per turn; code actions call the same tools as functions in a loop.

tooldesign.name: Prompt & Tool Controls
tooldesign.note: Controls trim tool output for cost; tool design shapes names, results and errors so the model chooses and self-corrects.

parallel.name: Agent Execution Graphs
parallel.note: An execution graph plans the whole workflow; parallel tool calls are the per-turn choice of which calls run together.

parallel.name: Parallel Sub-Agents with Isolated Context
parallel.note: Parallel tool calls run several tools inside one agent's context; parallel sub-agents give each piece its own context, so the raw results never meet.

idempotency.name: Action Policies and Approval Thresholds
idempotency.note: Zero trust decides whether an action is allowed; an idempotency key makes the allowed action safe to repeat.

idempotency.name: Agent Execution Graphs
idempotency.note: Graph nodes that replay after a crash need idempotent side effects.

idempotency.name: Timeouts, Circuit Breakers and Fallbacks
idempotency.note: Safe retries make one call repeatable; timeouts, breakers and fallbacks protect the whole system when a dependency keeps failing.

idempotency.name: Durable Execution and Checkpointing
idempotency.note: Durable workflows run activities at least once, so side-effecting activities still need idempotency keys.

idempotency.name: Human-in-the-Loop Checkpoints
idempotency.note: Approval decides whether an action runs; an idempotency key makes sure the approved action runs only once, even after retries.

idempotency.name: Incident Response and Trace Replay
idempotency.note: The duplicate-refund incident had a contributing cause: no idempotency key per order, so a repeated refund call was paid twice.

mcp.name: Action Policies and Approval Thresholds
mcp.note: Every MCP tool call should still pass the zero-trust policy gate; MCP standardises discovery and invocation.

mcp.name: MCP Tool Poisoning and Supply Chain
mcp.note: MCP makes tools pluggable, and every server’s tool descriptions become prompt text the model trusts.

mcp.name: A Plain SDK Loop
mcp.note: MCP lets tools written once be used from a plain loop or any framework, which reduces lock-in.

mcp.name: Browser Automation Agents
mcp.note: Playwright MCP exposes a browser to agents as tools that act on accessibility-tree references.

mcp.name: Tool Authentication and Scoped Permissions
mcp.note: MCP’s authorization rules say what a remote server must check; tool auth is how the agent obtains, scopes, stores and refreshes the per-user tokens it presents.

a2a.name: Agent Execution Graphs
a2a.note: Graphs coordinate agents you own; A2A hands a task to an agent you do not.

a2a.name: Google Agent Development Kit
a2a.note: ADK speaks A2A, so its agents can call and be called by agents built with other frameworks.

a2a.name: Agent Identity and Least Privilege
a2a.note: When agents call other agents, each hop should present its own identity and pass on the user through token exchange, so no agent borrows another’s rights.

toolsearch.name: Prompt & Tool Controls
toolsearch.note: Loading fewer tool definitions per call is one of the biggest token savings; tool search does it without losing access to the rest.

toolsearch.name: Sparse Keyword Search (BM25)
toolsearch.note: Tool search is retrieval over tool descriptions: BM25 matches their words, and embedding search matches their meaning.

toolsearch.name: Context Budgeting
toolsearch.note: Tool definitions are part of the context budget; deferring most of them frees room for history and retrieved facts.

toolsearch.name: MCP Tool Poisoning and Supply Chain
toolsearch.note: Search ranks tools by their descriptions, so a poisoned description stuffed with popular words can win searches it should not.

toolsearch.name: Agent Skills
toolsearch.note: Both keep context small with many capabilities: tool search finds tools, skills load procedures on demand.

toolauth.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
toolauth.note: MCP’s authorization rules say what a remote server must check; tool auth is how the agent obtains, scopes, stores and refreshes the per-user tokens it presents.

toolauth.name: Action Policies and Approval Thresholds
toolauth.note: Action policies decide whether a call is allowed; per-user, per-tool scoped tokens make sure the call can only touch what that user consented to.

toolauth.name: Data Exfiltration Through Tools
toolauth.note: Keeping tokens out of the prompt and scoping them to one user and one tool shrinks what an exfiltration attempt can reach or copy.

toolauth.name: Audit Trails and Explainability
toolauth.note: Delegated per-user tokens let the audit trail name the user behind every tool call.

skills.name: Procedural Memory
skills.note: Skills are hand-written procedures; procedural memory is procedures the agent learns and saves itself.

skills.name: Tool Search and Large Tool Sets
skills.note: Both keep context small with many capabilities: tool search finds tools, skills load procedures on demand.

skills.name: MCP Tool Poisoning and Supply Chain
skills.note: A third-party skill can carry hidden instructions, like a poisoned tool description; review before installing.

gifs.a2a: A travel agent reads an airline agent’s signed card, the task moves from WORKING to INPUT_REQUIRED for an aisle-or-window answer and back, then completes after 42 s with a PNR artifact.
gifs.fcall: A sequence diagram: the app sends a balance question with two tools, the model returns a get_balance tool_use with id toolu_01, the app returns the ₹18,250 result under the same id, and the model answers in 2 turns with 1 call.
gifs.idempotency: A ₹2,499 refund runs but its response is lost at the 10 s timeout; a retry without a key refunds twice (₹4,998), while a retry with the same key gets the stored result and refunds once.
gifs.mcp: A host runs three MCP clients connected to GitHub over Streamable HTTP and Postgres and filesystem servers over stdio; tools/list returns 14 tools with ttlMs 300000, and a query_orders error about ISO 8601 dates is fixed on retry.
gifs.parallel: Four KYC lookups run in sequence for 3,400 ms, then slide together to finish in 1,200 ms, and open_account starts after the join to finish at 1,600 ms.
gifs.skills: Thirty skills sit in the agent's context as names and descriptions, about 3,000 tokens. A customer disputes a ₹4,800 card charge, so only the chargeback skill loads and its deadline script runs. Correct procedure selection rises to 93 percent and cost per 1,000 tasks falls from ₹11,625 to ₹1,625.
gifs.toolauth: An eight-second animation titled Tool Auth. First, one shared API key sits in the agent's prompt, above a grid of 60 squares standing for Dhan Disha's 50,000 accounts; when the key leaks, every square turns red and a caption reads: 50,000 accounts, read and redeem, for 90 days. Next, the key is replaced by user U-1042's own token, kept in a vault rather than the prompt. On the right, the user signs in with OAuth 2.1 and PKCE and consents, the token is scoped to statements:read for 15 minutes, and a gateway attaches it so the model never sees it. The grid dims except for one green square, and the caption now reads: 1 account, read-only, 15 minutes. Finally, an injected instruction to redeem all units is blocked because the token is read-only, and an audit line records U-1042, get_statements, statements:read.
gifs.tooldesign: 48 tersely described tools pick the right tool 7 times in 10; 12 task-shaped tools with full descriptions get 10 of 10; then a result bar shrinks from 4,100 tokens to 380.
gifs.toolsearch: A library of 240 tools from 6 MCP servers. Loading them all costs 43,200 tokens a call and the agent often picks the wrong tool. With 4 common tools kept loaded and the rest deferred, the agent searches for “stop SIP mandate”, 5 matching tools load, and it calls cancel_sip_mandate at about 1,400 tokens a call.

header.lede: An agent is only as reliable as its tools: how a model calls them, how to design them, how to run them in parallel and retry them safely, how to find the right one among hundreds, and the open protocols that share tools and agents across applications.
